profiles.name: Fortress Commander
profiles.shortDescription: You prioritise strong barriers, chokepoints and early control.
profiles.description: Fortress Commanders want the first phase of collapse to be survivable through walls, high ground and defensible approaches. They accept that the strongest positions can need more supply discipline over time.
profiles.strength: Defensible perimeters and immediate threat control
profiles.compromise: May trade resource depth or easy access for stronger protection

profiles.name: Island Isolationist
profiles.shortDescription: You favour distance, separation and fewer approach routes.
profiles.description: Island Isolationists reduce contact with infected areas and hostile traffic by choosing places that are hard to reach. The price is slower movement, limited salvage and heavier reliance on what is already on site.
profiles.strength: Low exposure through remoteness and controlled approaches
profiles.compromise: Harder resupply, evacuation and outside contact

profiles.name: Community Builder
profiles.shortDescription: You focus on people, skills and renewable settlement life.
profiles.description: Community Builders see survival as a long-term group project. They value food systems, shared labour and governance, even when that means accepting more visible or less bunker-like locations.
profiles.strength: Long-term resilience through skills, food and cooperation
profiles.compromise: Larger groups can increase visibility and coordination pressure

profiles.name: Resource Planner
profiles.shortDescription: You prioritise dependable supplies, sustainability and long-term resilience.
profiles.description: Resource Planners look for places where food, water, medical basics and renewable supplies can keep a group alive after stored goods run down. They often accept less extreme isolation if the resource base is stronger.
profiles.compromise: Less emphasis on extreme isolation or immediate mobility

profiles.name: Systems Survivor
profiles.shortDescription: You are willing to use complex infrastructure if it improves resilience.
profiles.description: Systems Survivors accept engineered sites, technical maintenance and specialist knowledge when those systems provide protection, power, water or control. Their risk is that complexity becomes a burden without skilled people and spare parts.
profiles.compromise: Higher maintenance burden and dependency on expertise

profiles.name: Resilient Generalist
profiles.shortDescription: You balance defence, resources, isolation and people rather than maximising one axis.
profiles.description: Resilient Generalists avoid all-in strategies. They prefer bases with fewer severe weaknesses and enough flexibility to adapt as conditions change.
profiles.compromise: May miss the strongest specialist advantage in any single category
